lys.name: Lys
lys.desc: A young woman in hunter's leathers, fletching, watching you instead of the trees.
onDeath: Lys goes down still holding half a fletched arrow. Somewhere west, her brother will never hear that she almost came for him.

remarks.say: Thornwold's burning. My brother better have been clear of it.
You killed him. I understand why. I don't have to like it.
Leaving him like that, neither rested nor answered — that's its own kind of cruelty, I think.
He's at rest. No blood on it. That's the mercy I'd have chosen too.
A crown's just metal. Whatever you did with it, nobody starved for it.
Doors shut for good behind us. Feels right. Some things shouldn't be easy to walk back into.
Camp Gallows is close now. Some of me wants to run there today. Some of me knows better than to hope out loud.
Wet ground, soft footing. I don't like a wood I can't hear myself walk through.
Open moor. No cover for a hundred strides. I don't love being this easy to see.
Iron on the wind before we even crest the hill. This is Tamsin's country more than mine.
Barrows every way I look. Whatever sleeps under this ground, I'd rather not wake it.
Salt air. My father always said it ruins a good bowstring. He wasn't wrong.
Thin air, thin trail. Watch your footing more than the view up here.
So this is the city that started all of it. Doesn't look like much, for the weight it's carrying.
Three hollows quiet now, and none of them by fire. That's a road I can walk without flinching.
You've more than earned a place at my fire. Didn't think that would happen, and it did.
One more thing like that and I'm done following you. I only say a thing once.
I'm starting to wonder why I still walk beside you. Give me a reason before I stop wondering.
Thornwold's hollow rests now, not burned. My brother's company still has a camp to come home to.
Bargained, not burned, not rested outright. Thornwold keeps its dead quieter now. I will take quieter.
He is really coming home. I keep checking over my shoulder like I will spook it if I look too hard.
I marked his grave the way I mark a trail. So I could find him again, if that makes any sense to you.
No grave, no word. I have stopped asking out loud. Doesn't mean I have stopped asking.
Inside the palace walls now. Too many doors I can't see the other side of, for my liking.
You took the Regent's oil easy enough. I hope you know what you traded for it.
You told her no. Didn't think you had it in you, and I mean that as a compliment.
Four hundred years and he finally said it out loud. Some silences just need company to break.
Leave it. It isn't hunting — it's keeping something. We can go around.

leaves.say: He was still in there, and you knew it, and you did it anyway. I watched Thornwold burn from the ridge. I'm done.
I've watched you long enough to know what you are. I won't watch anymore.

topics.label: who are you
topics.say: Hunter's daughter. I've walked this wood since before I could spell my own name. Ask plain, I'll answer plain.

topics.label: what you're really out here for
topics.say: My brother went west to Thornwold a year gone — the Free Company, Camp Gallows, not a word sent home since. My father won't let me go after him. I'm done waiting on his permission.

topics.label: what you make of the gray
topics.say: Wolves that don't flinch from fire. Does that don't run. The wood's forgetting how to be afraid, and that troubles me worse than any tooth or claw.

topics.label: come with me
topics.say: ...Fine. Somebody ought to watch your back better than you do.

topics.label: wait here
topics.say: Watching the trees only needs one set of eyes. I'll be here.

topics.label: ask her to come back
topics.say: No. You had your chance to get him clear, and Thornwold burned with him still inside it. I'll walk this wood alone before I walk beside that again.

topics.label: ask her to come back
topics.say: ...All right. Didn't say I'd forgotten. Said I'd come.

topics.label: ask her to come back
topics.say: Not yet. You know where to find me when that changes.

topics.label: ask what she's not saying
topics.say: My mother used to say the wood forgives everything but waiting too long. I didn't believe her till my brother left. Don't wait too long on what you love, either.

topics.label: ask why she's gone quiet
topics.say: You want it plain? I think you'd walk past a starving thing in the road if it slowed you down. I've seen you do it.

topics.label: tell her to go to him herself
topics.say: Word comes: he's alive, camped with the Free Company at Camp Gallows. You tell her to go to him herself, whatever it costs. She's quiet a moment, then nods, like she'd been waiting to hear it.

topics.label: call her brother a deserter
topics.say: Word comes: he's alive, camped with the Free Company at Camp Gallows. You call him a deserter not worth chasing. Something in her face closes like a shutter, and she doesn't argue the point.

topics.label: ask after her brother
topics.say: He's home. She doesn't say much about it, just stands in the doorway a while, watching him sleep like he might vanish if she looks away.

topics.label: ask after her brother
topics.say: She buried him herself, east of Camp Gallows, and marked the spot the way hunters mark a trail — so she could find it again. She doesn't cry where you can see.

topics.label: ask after her brother
topics.say: No grave, no word, nothing. She's stopped asking after him out loud. You catch her some nights, still watching the eastern road anyway.

topics.label: ask why she never went herself
topics.say: I got as far as the Thornwold treeline once, a year before you ever came. Heard the Company's fires through the trees, and turned back. Told myself it was the wood. It wasn't.

topics.label: ask what stopped her
topics.say: If I'd found him and he told me to stay lost, that would have been the end of hoping on him. I'd rather carry not-knowing than that. I have never said this out loud before now.

topics.label: let her teach you to read the ground
topics.say: Take this much, at least — a broken twig, a turned stone, a print gone soft at the edge. Ground talks, if you know where to look. Watch where I'm looking, not where I'm walking.

topics.label: pay to spread word of her brother
topics.say: That's real coin, not a promise. Riders will carry Cal's name down every road between here and Thornwold faster than either of us could walk it. I didn't expect this from you. Thank you.

topics.label: leave it there
topics.say: Mind your footing. This wood doesn't forgive twice.

osk.name: Brother Osk
osk.desc: A gray-robed novice sweeping the same flagstone, verses half-remembered on his lips.
onDeath: Brother Osk goes still mid-verse, the words unfinished — the same as the rite he came here to learn, and never will now.

remarks.say: Fenmarch's burning. My mother's grave is under that water somewhere. I can't — I need a moment.
No rite. No verse. Just — ended. I keep waiting to feel it was right.
Leaving him neither rested nor answered is the exact wound the Church exists to close. We didn't close it.
He's at rest. Say what you will of the road there — the door opened, and grief went out through it. The teaching, proven true.
A broken crown won't trouble the dead much. What troubles them is being forgotten. That crown wasn't forgetting anyone.
Sealed doors again. I understand the reeve's reasons. I don't have to agree with every one of them.
Rough company, this Free Company. I'll say a verse for whoever needs one and try not to judge the rest.
Reedholm. I know these stilts better than I know my own two feet. Careful where you put yours.
The Watch keeps good order up here. Order isn't the same as peace, but it's not nothing either.
Cinderhall smells of ash even from the road. I don't think that's only the forges.
Barrowmere. So many kept graves in one place. The Keepers do good work, whatever else gets said of them.
Gullhaven. Salt air, hard people. I like it more than I expected to.
This high, even the verses feel thinner. Or maybe that's just the air.
Marrowgate. Four hundred years of unrested grief, and a throne built right on top of it. Lord.
Three doors opened properly now, three graces given air. More good than I've managed in a year of trying.
I didn't expect to trust anyone this quickly again. Thank you for that, whether you meant to earn it or not.
If it happens again, I'm gone — I mean that, and I don't say things like that lightly.
I keep telling myself there's a reason for what you do. I'm running out of ways to believe it.
Fenmarch's drowned nave rests easy now. I said a verse for it myself, badly, same as always.
Bargained, they are saying, not rested proper. It is something. The Church teaches something is often enough.
They are at rest. I said the rite myself, and only cracked once. I think that means I am getting better at this.
They burned with the nave. I have not been able to say a verse since, not even a bad one.
Inside the palace now. I keep expecting someone to ask what right we have to be here.
You took her oil. I understand why. I still had to look away when you did it.
You told the Regent no. Some doors are worth staying shut. I did not think you would agree with me.
Four hundred years of silence, and he finally said the words. That is a rite too, in its way.

leaves.say: You burned it. My family, the nave, all of it. I have nothing left to say to you.
I came to this Church to be better than my worst assumptions about people. Standing next to you keeps proving them right. I'm done.

topics.label: who are you
topics.say: Brother Osk, of the Gray Church — a novice still, whatever the robe suggests. I'm told my verses need work. I'm told a lot of things.

topics.label: your own family
topics.say: The water took my family in Fenmarch, before I ever wore this gray. I came here to learn what to say over the drowned. Nobody's finished teaching me yet.

topics.label: why the Church, and why you
topics.say: Someone has to sit with grief and mean it. I wasn't much good at anything else, so — here I am, still learning to mean it properly.

topics.label: what you make of the gray
topics.say: Grief that's never given air festers. That's the whole of Church teaching on it, and I believe every word — I just don't always know how to open the door.

topics.label: come with me
topics.say: ...Truly? Then — yes. Purpose is easier to find walking than kneeling, some days.

topics.label: wait here
topics.say: I'll keep this ground quiet while you're gone. It's what I'm for, mostly.

topics.label: ask him to come back
topics.say: No. You burned the nave with my family still unrested inside it. I have no verse left that forgives that, and I've stopped looking for one.

topics.label: ask him to come back
topics.say: ...The Church teaches forgiveness. I'm meant to practice what I preach, badly as I preach it. I'll come.

topics.label: ask him to come back
topics.say: Not yet. I need to believe it before I follow it. Give me more than words.

topics.label: ask what he really believes
topics.say: Some nights I'm not sure the old king even hears the verses. I say them anyway. Faith, near as I can tell, is doing it anyway.

topics.label: ask why he won't meet your eye
topics.say: Because I keep hoping you'll surprise me, and you keep not doing it. That's a hard thing to say to someone's face. There. Said it.

topics.label: tell him his verses are worth saying
topics.say: Word reaches the chapel: his family's found, in the drowned nave, past hoping for but not past grieving. You tell him his verses are worth saying, badly or not. He almost smiles.

topics.label: tell him the rites are superstition
topics.say: Word reaches the chapel: his family's found, in the drowned nave, past hoping for but not past grieving. You tell him the old rites are just superstition. He goes very quiet, and doesn't answer.

topics.label: ask after his family
topics.say: They're at rest. He said the rite himself, voice cracking on the third verse, and didn't stop. I think he's a priest now, whatever the Church calls it officially.

topics.label: ask after his family
topics.say: The nave burned with them still in it. He hasn't quoted a verse since. I'm not sure he believes in doors anymore, open or shut.

topics.label: ask what he really remembers of that day
topics.say: I wasn't there. Sent off for dry wood on some errand nobody even remembers giving me now. I have never told a living soul I sometimes wonder if that's the only reason I'm still here.

topics.label: ask if he blames himself
topics.say: Every night, some, if I'm honest — and I'm trying, for once, to be. The verses I'm learning are as much for me as for anyone drowned. Thank you for asking it plain.

topics.label: let him teach you the steadying litany
topics.say: Here, then — the litany the old priest said before hard work, not holy exactly, just steady. Say it under your breath and your hand won't shake when it matters most.

topics.label: back him against the priory's counsel
topics.say: I didn't ask you to cross the Priory for me. You did it anyway, plain and public, and they'll remember whose voice said it. That costs you something I can't give back to you.

topics.label: that's enough for now
topics.say: Go gently. The gray doesn't need help from us to be cruel.

tamsin.name: Tamsin
tamsin.desc: Forge-scarred hands at the second anvil, keeping time with the smith's without missing a stroke.
onDeath: Tamsin goes down at the second anvil, mid-swing. The smith will have to find new hands for that hammer.

remarks.say: Cinderhall's burning. Whatever's left of the truth about that mine burns with it. Convenient, that.
Good. Grief that won't quit gets put down, same as anything else that won't quit.
You walked away and settled nothing. That's the one option I'd have talked you out of, if you'd asked.
He's quiet now. Didn't need killing after all. Fine — I'll take an ending that doesn't cost a fight, when one's on offer.
Broke the crown. Good — less for the next fool to fight over.
Sealed for good. That's a door that'll hold. I checked the hinges myself.
Free Company work, this ground. Mercenaries. I've sharpened enough of their blades to know their word's worth exactly what they're paid.
Wet ground ruins good steel fast. Whatever you're carrying, dry it tonight.
Watch country. Say what you like about rules — their gear's always in good repair. I respect that.
Cinderhall. Home ground, near enough. I know this air. Iron and old smoke.
Barrows everywhere you look. Keepers guard the dead like the dead are still paying them. Maybe they are.
Salt eats steel worse than anything. Remind me to check every blade we're carrying before we leave.
Cold enough up here to crack a bad weld. Whoever forged your gear better have known what they were doing.
Marrowgate. Big walls, soft hands, near as I can tell. We'll see if that holds up.
Three hollows settled without burning a one of them. Didn't think that was the harder road. Turns out it was.
You've earned my back in a fight. That's not a small thing, coming from me.
One more like that and I'm gone. I don't give second warnings, only first ones.
I don't waste time on people I don't trust. I'm starting to wonder why I'm still wasting it on you.
Cinderhall's settled without burning. Did not think that was possible down there. Good to be wrong.
Bargained instead of burned. Not clean, but it holds. I can live with not-clean, if it holds.
Whoever lied about that collapse answered for it. I did not need to swing a hammer. Strange feeling.
I let it lie. Chasing it was not bringing her back. Took me long enough to admit that plainly.
They sold out the men still working that mine. For coin. I do not have words for that. I have a hammer.
Inside the palace. Big walls, soft floors. I keep waiting for someone to ask us to leave.
You took her oil and her bargain both. Fine. Just do not forget whose name goes on it after.
You said no to a Regent's offer. Did not flinch either, near as I could tell. Good.
He said it plain, finally. Four hundred years is a long time to swing at nothing.

leaves.say: You sold out the miners. The same mine that killed my mother, and you sold out the men still working it for coin. We're done.
I don't fight beside people I can't trust at my back. That's you now. Find someone else.

topics.label: who are you
topics.say: Smith's apprentice. Ask me about steel and I'll talk your ear off. Ask me about anything else, keep it short.

topics.label: what you actually want
topics.say: Ask the smith and she'll tell you not to say 'mine' near me. I'm saying it anyway: the Hundred came down on my mother in the Iron Downs, and nobody's ever given me a straight answer why.

topics.label: what you make of the gray
topics.say: Grief's not complicated. Something's wrong, you find what's wrong, you fix it or you burn it. People make it complicated because plain answers scare them.

topics.label: come with me
topics.say: Good. I've been itching to hit something that isn't an anvil.

topics.label: wait here
topics.say: Fine. Don't get yourself killed doing something I could've done faster.

topics.label: ask her to come back
topics.say: No. You sold out men working the same mine that killed my mother, for coin, and you want me to forget that. I don't forget. Ever.

topics.label: ask her to come back
topics.say: ...You've done enough to earn a second look. Don't waste it.

topics.label: ask her to come back
topics.say: Not yet. Show me, don't tell me.

topics.label: ask what really drives her
topics.say: I was twelve when the Hundred came down and they carried what was left of my mother out of that shaft. I've been counting blows ever since — needed something I could measure.

topics.label: ask what she thinks of you
topics.say: You want it straight? I think you talk more than you act, and I've got no use for people like that. There. Straight.

topics.label: tell her to make them answer for it
topics.say: The truth about the mine comes out at last, uglier than she guessed. You tell her to make whoever's responsible answer for it. She nods once, already working out how.

topics.label: tell her chasing it wastes good iron
topics.say: The truth about the mine comes out at last, uglier than she guessed. You tell her chasing it further wastes good iron and better time. Something in her jaw sets hard.

topics.label: ask about the mine
topics.say: Whoever lied about that collapse has answered for it now, her way — plain, and final. She doesn't talk about it much. Doesn't need to.

topics.label: ask about the mine
topics.say: She let it lie, in the end. Said carrying it further wouldn't carry her mother back. First time I've heard her sound tired instead of angry.

topics.label: ask about the miners
topics.say: The miners got sold out to the Ironbound for a tidy sum, truth and all, buried under it. She hasn't said a word since she heard. That's worse than shouting.

topics.label: ask what she still expects, some days
topics.say: Some mornings I still listen for her boots on the forge steps. Twenty years gone and some fool part of me hasn't caught up with the rest. Never told the smith that. Never told anyone.

topics.label: ask why she never told the smith
topics.say: She'd worry, and worrying doesn't temper steel. Counting does. So I count, and I don't tell her, and most days that's enough to get the hammer swinging again.

topics.label: let her re-temper your blade
topics.say: Hand it over. Won't take long done right. There — feel that edge now. It won't turn on you when it matters most, and neither will I.

topics.label: cross the Ironbound to back her question
topics.say: You put the question to the Ironbound chapter yourself, plain and public, and didn't back down when they didn't like it. They'll mark your name for it. I'm not going to say thank you. I don't have to.

topics.label: that's enough for now
topics.say: Watch your footing. I'm not carrying you back.

vell.name: Vell
vell.desc: A traveller in road-worn gray, a book open by the fire, unbothered by much.
onDeath: Vell falls with the book still open on their knee, a sentence half-copied that no one will ever finish reading.

remarks.say: Hollowbrook's burning, and with it every record the Keepers never finished copying. That is not a small loss.
A death, unrecorded by any rite. History will remember only that he stopped being a problem. Poor epitaph.
An unfinished story. I dislike those more than sad endings. At least a sad ending is an ending.
Properly rested, properly recorded. That's the kind of ending that actually holds.
You broke it. Four hundred years of history, and you broke it. I have opinions about this I am choosing not to share yet.
Sealed away from study forever, most likely. A scholar's small grief, next to everything else that happened there.
Mercenary country. Poor record-keeping, excellent gossip. I'll take what I can get.
Fenmarch keeps its history underwater, apparently. I do hope it kept it readable.
Wardmoor's archive is meant to be excellent. I intend to find out, given half a chance.
The Ironbound burn what they don't like. I try not to think too hard about what that's cost the Downs' history.
Barrowmere. The Keepers' Hall is here somewhere. I have — reasons to want to see it.
Gullhaven keeps its records in the harbormaster's memory, near as I can tell. Frustrating, and probably more accurate than paper.
St. Ashwyn's Perch. Old enough to remember things properly, if anyone up here still bothers to ask it.
Marrowgate.
Three rites completed properly, three records worth keeping. I'm almost tempted to write this down as it happens, for once.
I don't extend trust for free. Consider this the exception, not the rule.
One more incident like that and I revise my opinion of you permanently. Consider this your only warning.
I am reconsidering several earlier assessments of your character. None of the revisions favor you.
Hollowbrook's barrow-court rests, properly recorded, I hope. I intend to check the record myself.
Bargained — the mounds settle for less than rest. An imprecise ending. I dislike those. It will have to do.
So it is found. My name is not in it — my grandfather's is. Close enough, I suppose.
I would have told you myself, eventually. Being dragged into the light is not the same as choosing it.
Inside the palace that exiled my line. I find I have opinions I am choosing not to voice yet.
You took the Regent's oil. I wonder if you understand yet whose furniture you are burning.
You refused her. I confess I did not expect that, and I dislike being wrong this pleasantly.
Four hundred years unrecorded, and now it is said aloud. I intend to write this one down properly.

leaves.say: You broke the one thing that might have named me honestly, and I no longer trust you to carry what's left of the truth. I'll carry it myself.
I've reconsidered the wisdom of this arrangement entirely. Goodbye.

topics.label: who are you
topics.say: A wandering scholar, of sorts. I read old stones for a living, when the living pays. Ask me anything — I may even answer truthfully.

topics.label: what you're really after
topics.say: A particular kind of truth, buried in a particular kind of ledger. I'll say no more than that until I trust you a little further.

topics.label: why you go quiet at 'Marrowgate'
topics.say: Do I? I hadn't noticed. Some cities aren't kind to certain names. Leave it there, for now.

topics.label: what you make of the gray
topics.say: Four hundred years of neglected rites, come due all at once. Not a curse. An unpaid debt — and debts don't forget the way people do.

topics.label: come with me
topics.say: ...An excellent notion, actually. I do my best thinking while walking, and my worst while paying for a room.

topics.label: wait here
topics.say: I'll mind the ledgers. Someone ought to, and it clearly isn't going to be you.

topics.label: ask them to come back
topics.say: ...Curiosity outweighs pride, in the end. It usually does, with me. I'll come.

topics.label: ask them to come back
topics.say: Not yet. I'd rather finish being right about you before I forgive you for it.

topics.label: ask what they're hiding
topics.say: The truth, since you've earned it: I'm Marrowgate's own blood, exiled before I could walk. The ledger in Hollowbrook proves it. I'd rather you heard it from me than the throne.

topics.label: ask what they think of you
topics.say: I think you handle the truth the way a child handles a knife — carelessly, and someone always ends up cut.

topics.label: tell them the truth is worth knowing
topics.say: The ledger surfaces at last, every line damning or vindicating, depending on the reader. You tell them the truth deserves to be known, whatever it costs. They go still, then nod.

topics.label: tell them to burn the ledger
topics.say: The ledger surfaces at last, every line damning or vindicating, depending on the reader. You tell them to burn it and be done with the whole business. Something in their face closes over.

topics.label: ask about the ledger
topics.say: The secret got out before Vell ever chose to tell it — dragged into the light at the worst possible moment. They haven't forgiven whoever did that. Might not forgive themselves either.

topics.label: ask if they've ever been to Marrowgate
topics.say: Once. Years before I met you, plain gray, nobody looking twice. I stood in the market square, looked up at the palace, and did not go in. I have never told anyone that either.

topics.label: ask why they turned back that day
topics.say: I wasn't ready to know what I'd do, standing in that hall with that name behind me. I'm still not entirely sure. I'd rather you knew that about me before either of us finds out.

topics.label: let them annotate your memory
topics.say: Hold still — this won't hurt, and it won't show. Just recall the shape of what you want to keep, and I'll mark the parts worth keeping. The right fact will surface when you need it.

topics.label: swear to keep their name out of it
topics.say: You gave your word, plainly, that whatever that ledger says stays between the two of us unless I choose otherwise. I don't extend trust for free, remember. Consider this noted. And remembered.

topics.label: that's enough for now
topics.say: Do try not to lose anything important while I'm not looking.

lys_whistle.name: a bone hunting-whistle
lys_whistle.hint: two low notes, and somewhere in the trees, she'll hear them.

osk_verse_scrap.name: a verse in an unsteady hand
osk_verse_scrap.hint: his own hand, mistakes and all — he wanted you to have it right, even wrong.

tamsin_hammer_charm.name: a thumbnail-small forge-charm
tamsin_hammer_charm.hint: her mother's iron. She doesn't explain further, and you don't ask.

vell_cipher_key.name: a strip of vellum, a cipher in hand
vell_cipher_key.hint: notes in Vell's own hand — might unlock more of theirs, if you find any.

stages.text: He's buried east of Camp Gallows, in Thornwold. Grief, not victory — but it's finished.
He's alive and found. What happens next in Thornwold isn't yours to force.
You're in Thornwold. Find Camp Gallows and ask after him by name.
Ask after Lys's brother at Camp Gallows, in Thornwold west of the Vale.
His family is found in the drowned nave. What happens next in Fenmarch isn't yours to force.
You're in Fenmarch. Ask after Osk's family at the drowned nave, near Reedholm.
Ask Osk about his family, then find Fenmarch east of the Vale.
She's let the mine lie, in her own way. There's nothing more it can take from her now.
She knows the truth about the collapse. What she does with it in Cinderhall is hers to choose.
You're in the Iron Downs. Ask after the collapsed mine at Cinderhall.
Ask Tamsin about the mine, then find Cinderhall in the Iron Downs, past Thornwold.
You're in Hollowbrook. Ask after the Keepers' Hall and the ledger it holds.
Vell goes quiet at the name Marrowgate. The Keepers' Hall in Hollowbrook might hold why.
Ask Vell about Marrowgate, then find the Keepers' Hall in Hollowbrook, north past Fenmarch.

epilogue.text: Lys never got the chance to find her brother. Nobody else went looking either.
Lys walked out of your company on the road and never came back to it.
Lys brought her brother home to the Vale, and the hunter's camp is loud again, for the first time in years.
Lys buried her brother east of Camp Gallows and marked the spot the way hunters mark a trail.
Lys still watches the eastern road some evenings, though she's stopped saying why.
Lys stayed at the hunter's camp, watching the treeline, and never learned how the rest of it ended.
By the end Lys called you the steadiest thing on a road she never expected to walk this far down.
Lys still walks beside you, but she watches you now the way she watches strange ground — carefully, from a distance.
Brother Osk's verse went unfinished. The chapel lit a candle and did not say why.
Brother Osk left your company on the road, verses and all, and did not send word after.
Brother Osk said the rite over his own family himself, and the Church quietly stopped calling him a novice.
Brother Osk has not quoted a verse since Fenmarch burned. He still wears the gray.
Brother Osk stayed in the chapel, tending a grief that was never quite his own to carry alone.
Brother Osk stopped calling himself a novice somewhere around you, though the Church never made it official.
Osk still says the rites when you ask him to, but he has stopped explaining them to you, and you have stopped asking why.
Tamsin's hammer hangs unclaimed at the Vale forge. Nobody there swings it as hard.
Tamsin walked out of your company and didn't look back to see if you noticed.
Tamsin got her answer about the mine, and made whoever lied about it answer in turn.
Tamsin let the mine keep its dead in the end. She sounds tired more than angry now, when it comes up.
